Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at Example 1 (2024-11-13):
- History: Price range 62.28 to 68.02, currently at 67.53 (near the high end)
- Sentiment: Mixed, last few values: 0.00, 0.67, 1.00, 0.67, 0.50, 0.00, 0.00
- Model forecast: Starts at 66.59, gradually increasing to 71.52
- True outcome: Starts at 66.31, gradually increasing to 69.47

Comparing model vs true:
- At day 1: 66.59 vs 66.31 (model +0.28 too high)
- Day 5: 68.59 vs 68.13 (+0.46)
- Day 10: 68.89 vs 68.47 (+0.42)
- Day 15: 69.13 vs 68.49 (+0.64)
- Day 20: 69.41 vs 69.93 (-0.52)
- Day 25: 69.39 vs 67.69 (-1.70)

Looking at the pattern - the model seems to be forecasting more gradual, smoother increases than the true outcomes which have more volatility. But more importantly, let me look at the relationship with sentiment.

Looking at Example 2 (2024-09-26):
- History: Price range 62.82 to 70.43, currently at 65.24
- Sentiment: [0.67, 0.33, 0.67, 0.33, 0.67, 0.67, 0.00, 0.33, 0.33, 0.00, 0.67, 0.67, 0.33, 0.33, 0.00, 1.00, 0.33, 1.00]


- Model forecast: Starts at 66.42, trending downward to 65.52
- True outcome: Starts at 66.52, trending downward to 65.75
